findings.body:
**Keep the earlier saved timeout when systemd ignores an empty assignment.**

If a saved service declares `TimeoutStartSec=10min` and then an empty `TimeoutStartSec=`, systemd 255 keeps the ten-minute value. This branch clears it. With a pinned 60-second timeout, recovery then gives `systemctl start` only 120 seconds. A healthy eight-minute start times out after the mask is removed and before the activators are restored. Treat an empty value as an ignored assignment, like other invalid values. Keep the pinned fallback when no valid saved value exists. ([raw.githubusercontent.com](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/systemd/systemd/v255/src/core/load-fragment.c))
findings.title: Keep the earlier saved timeout when systemd ignores an empty assignment.

findings.body:
**Check activation against the restored service’s type.**

Recovery starts the saved service file but selects the state check from the pinned template. If the pinned service is `oneshot` and the saved service is `simple`, a saved service that exits successfully before `show` can report `inactive`. Recovery accepts that state and releases the timer even though the saved service was active. Read `Type` from the loaded restored unit. Require `active` for a saved simple service and retain the completed-oneshot allowance for a saved oneshot. ([raw.githubusercontent.com](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/systemd/systemd/v255/src/core/dbus-service.c))
findings.title: Check activation against the restored service’s type.

findings.body:
**Reject NUL bytes before validating drop-in directives.**

`splitlines()` and systemd 255 disagree on NUL: systemd treats it as a line boundary. The adapter can skip an entire apparent comment line while systemd reads a separate `TimeoutStartSec` assignment from it. That invalidates the preflight bound even when the declared directory, file ownership and mode all pass. Reject NUL in drop-in text before checking the directive allowlist. Normal LF and CRLF environment drop-ins can still pass. ([raw.githubusercontent.com](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/systemd/systemd/v255/src/basic/fileio.c))
findings.title: Reject NUL bytes before validating drop-in directives.

findings.body:
**Correct the recovery sequence’s description of snapshot validation.**

`unit-adapter.py` already validates the schema, exact owned paths, metadata and activation states at Lines 1407–1459. This step says the validator does not exist, contrary to Lines 6–11 of this document. Name the implemented checks and keep the separate caveat that their host behavior still needs live proof.
findings.title: Correct the recovery sequence’s description of snapshot validation.

findings.body:
**Recheck saved activator paths before removing the mask.**

`install` and `restore` check the activator files, but neither activation method repeats that check before release. If host maintenance replaces a one-minute timer with a one-hour timer at the same path after staging, discovery can still report the same path and file type. The next reload loads the changed timer. Forward completion uses the old deadline, and recovery can report success without restoring the saved timer bytes. Compare the activator files and enablement links with the snapshot while the mask is still in place. If they match, the existing release order can proceed.







Also applies to: 1956-1956
findings.title: Recheck saved activator paths before removing the mask.

findings.body:
**The timer bound omits RandomizedDelaySec, and the validator does not reject it.**

`_timer_schedule_seconds` derives the completion bound only from `OnCalendar`, `OnUnitActiveSec`, `OnUnitInactiveSec`, and `AccuracySec`. A `RandomizedDelaySec=` value in the timer template therefore does not change the returned bound. `validate_unit_template` checks only that `.service` and `.path` templates contain `@CRQ_ROOT@`. It does not inspect timer directives. A timer with `RandomizedDelaySec=2h` passes the validator and the bound check. Preflight can then admit the original deadline while systemd delays the healthy second activation beyond it. Account for the directive in the bound, or refuse timers that declare it.
findings.title: The timer bound omits RandomizedDelaySec, and the validator does not reject it.

findings.body:
**Reject non-object `package.json` values before calling `.get`.**

If a clean checkout contains `package.json` with the valid JSON value `null`, Line 127 succeeds, but Line 130 raises `AttributeError`. The handler at Line 409 does not catch that exception. A `--json` invocation therefore emits a traceback instead of a JSON error.

Check `isinstance(package, dict)` and raise `BuildError` before reading `packageManager`. Keep the existing pin validation for object manifests.

As per coding guidelines, “In machine mode (`--json`) stderr stays empty.”
findings.title: Reject non-object `package.json` values before calling `.get`.

findings.body:
**Stop command descendants before releasing the checkout lock.**

If `pnpm run build` times out while a compiler child remains active, `subprocess.run` kills only the direct process. CPython's timeout path does not terminate the process group. ([raw.githubusercontent.com](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/python/cpython/3.11/Lib/subprocess.py))

At `apps/crq-python/ops/build-runner.py`, Line 80 raises `BuildError`, and Line 270 releases the checkout lock. A second build can then remove `dist/` or install dependencies while the first compiler still writes.

Start commands in an isolated process group. On timeout or cancellation, terminate that group and complete shutdown before releasing the checkout lock. Preserve normal waiting behavior for successful commands.
findings.title: Stop command descendants before releasing the checkout lock.

findings.body:
**Sync the marker directory when acquiring and releasing admission.**

Syncing the token file does not guarantee that the marker's directory entry survives a power loss. If the host loses power after switching but before verification, it can reboot without the admission hold. An unsynced removal can also leave a stale hold after reboot. ([man7.org](https://man7.org/linux/man-pages/man2/fsync.2.html?utm_source=openai))

Sync the parent directory after creation and removal. If either sync fails, report that the admission transition could not be verified.






Also applies to: 459-459
findings.title: Sync the marker directory when acquiring and releasing admission.

findings.body:
**Prevent `status` from combining observations from different deployments.**

`status` can read HEAD A and see no marker just before another deploy starts. If that deploy switches to B and restarts the same timer before the unit query, `status` returns `ok: true` for A while B is live.

Take the deploy and controller locks while reading HEAD, the marker, and trigger states. If a lock is busy, report that status cannot be verified during the transition.
findings.title: Prevent `status` from combining observations from different deployments.

findings.body:
**Refuse before admission if the runtime entry is missing.**

`measure_cq_bin` records `exists=False` for a missing non-placeholder entry. Preflight accepts that measurement and switches. The post-switch check then fails, and rollback fails the same check after restoring HEAD. This leaves admission held for owner recovery.

Reject a missing non-placeholder entry before claiming the hold. Keep the explicit placeholder case and the post-switch check for entries that disappear later.
findings.title: Refuse before admission if the runtime entry is missing.

findings.body:
**Apply the queue drain deadline to the probes.**

With `--drain-deadline-s 15`, two liveness probes that each time out after 30 seconds delay the deadline check for about a minute. `drain_check` visits both runs before returning. The poll sleep can also exceed the remaining budget.

Pass the remaining budget through `drain_check` to each probe and clamp the sleep to that budget. If time expires before the runbook proves the queue drained, retain the hold and report recovery required.
findings.title: Apply the queue drain deadline to the probes.

findings.body:
**Require the admission hold at both checkout switches.**

The forward path checks ownership before stopping triggers. The rollback path checks it before draining. If an operator removes or replaces the marker during either drain, the run can still call `helper.switch`. The supplied helper checks unit inactivity, not marker ownership.

Recheck ownership at both switch boundaries. Serialize supported marker changes with that check and switch. If ownership is lost, do not switch or remove a foreign marker.






Also applies to: 1146-1146
findings.title: Require the admission hold at both checkout switches.

findings.body:
**Print the receipt location when marker creation only partly succeeds.**

If exclusive creation succeeds but the token write leaves an empty marker, the runbook retains the marker and tells the owner to verify that it contains the full token. That check cannot succeed. The exception also carries no record, so the CLI prints `run_dir: null` even though the recovery receipt already exists.

Include the run directory, marker path, and ownership observation in the exit-3 result. Distinguish an incomplete write from a confirmed foreign marker. Apply the same reporting when rollback cannot persist its new hold.
findings.title: Print the receipt location when marker creation only partly succeeds.

findings.body:
**Make the run directory durable before claiming admission.**

`durable_write` syncs the receipt and the run directory. It does not sync the record base that contains the new run directory entry. If the record base is on a separate filesystem, a power loss can leave the host held but lose the entire run directory, including the prior SHA and trigger state. ([man7.org](https://man7.org/linux/man-pages/man2/fsync.2.html?utm_source=openai))

Sync the record base after creating the run directory. If the invocation creates the record base, persist its directory entry too. Do not claim admission if either step fails.
findings.title: Make the run directory durable before claiming admission.
